Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Fifteen youth startups receive GH¢210,000 in seed funding under compassion business challenge Source : Maud Adu 21 November 2026 9:26am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Fifteen young entrepreneurs have been awarded a combined GH¢210,000 in seed capital under the second edition of the Compassion Business Challenge, as stakeholders push youth entrepreneurship as a practical response to Ghana’s job crunch.
The initiative, run by Compassion International Ghana in partnership with organisations including LeadAfrique International and the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA), combines startup grants with business training, mentorship, and field monitoring. Tackling Youth Unemployment Through Enterprise
Speaking on the rationale behind the partnership, Letitia Ohene-Effah, Co-Founder of LeadAfrique International, pointed to the scale of youth exclusion from education and employment in Ghana, stressing that young people need practical skills to contribute meaningfully to the economy.
"First and foremost, if you look at Ghana, over 2 million of our young people are either not in school, and they're not in employment either, and we need to be able to give them the necessary skills that is required for them to be able to positively impact the economy that we live in," she said. Mentorship and Monitoring Beyond the Pitch
According to organisers, about 70 young applicants initially entered the second cohort, with just over 60 selected for training, capacity building, internships, and coaching.
Fifteen finalists reached the final pitch Overall winner Emmanuel Sabi of Sabi Bottles took home GH¢40,000, the first runner-up received GH¢30,000, and the second runner-up walked away with GH¢20,000. The remaining 12 finalists each received GH¢10,000 to support their ventures.
Rashidatu Iddrisah, Manager of Program Support at Compassion International Ghana, said this edition introduced deliberate business mentorship, pairing participants with established entrepreneurs to help them navigate startup hurdles, while keeping non-finalists connected to mentors. She added that the Ghana Enterprises Agency will partner with organisers to periodically visit and monitor participants' business centres.
"This time we'll be very intentional about bringing on board business mentors. So successful entrepreneurs who are into various forms of businesses who have run businesses and are successful to hold them by hand and then direct them, help them go through their, navigate through their challenges of the challenges startups usually face," Iddrisah noted.
Winner Draws on Flooding Experience Emerging as the 2026 Cohort 2 winner, Sabi said he entered the competition with strong confidence after prior experience with a challenge at the University of Cape Coast earlier in the year, noting that firsthand familiarity with flooding and its effects shaped his conviction that his business concept would succeed.
"So the moment I saw this link to our apply, I thought myself before that that the moment I will win. Because as you can experience this year 2026, if you a student at University of Cape Coast or University of Cape, you will know the consequence, the effect of flooding," he said. "So and by God grace I am here as a winner for 2026 entrepreneurship challenge Cohort 2."
